summary: University Hospital of Wales is run by Cardiff and Vale University Health Board, so your first step is the NHS Wales 'Listening to People' complaint route with the Health Board. If their answer is not enough, you can usually go to the Public Services Ombudsman for Wales after giving the Health Board a chance to reply; compensation in Wales can also be considered through the NHS redress process arising from the complaint, and you can get free help from Llais plus your records from the Health Records Department.

steps.body: Cardiff and Vale University Health Board
steps.what: University Hospital of Wales is part of Cardiff and Vale University Health Board in NHS Wales, so this is a public NHS Wales complaint. The Health Board says to raise concerns with the staff involved first; if that does not resolve it, use its 'Listening to People' complaints process by phone, email, post, or its downloadable complaints form. The newer Welsh Government page says concerns raised after 31 March 2026 follow 'Listening to People', while older pages still refer to 'Putting Things Right'.
steps.deadline: "You can take up to 12 months to raise a concern or complaint. However, it is best to talk to someone as soon as possible."
missing: Whether the patient has already complained to the Health Board

steps.what: If the Health Board's complaint answer is not good enough, the independent body is the Public Services Ombudsman for Wales. Its official pages say it is very unlikely to help unless you complained to the organisation first and gave it time to reply; its fact sheet says 12 weeks is a reasonable time for a final reply and complaints should usually reach the Ombudsman within a year of knowing about the issue.
steps.deadline: "you complained to us within a year of knowing about the issue"
requires: Complaint to Cardiff and Vale University Health Board first
Usually allow the Health Board time to give a final reply; "12 weeks is a reasonable time"
steps.appliesIf: NHS/public care in Wales and the provider complaint has not resolved the matter.
alternatives: Continue with compensation/redress or legal claim routes if harm compensation is sought

steps.what: For harm from NHS care in Wales, compensation can arise through the NHS Wales complaints/redress process rather than only by a separate court claim. Official NHS Wales Shared Services pages say claims for compensation are made once a concern from a complaint or patient-safety incident occurs, and NHS organisations must investigate to assess whether there is qualifying liability and therefore a right to compensation.
requires: A concern/complaint or patient-safety incident about NHS care
missing: Whether the patient wants to seek financial compensation
Whether the Health Board has opened a redress investigation
Details of losses such as wages and travel

sources.quote: Claims for compensation are made once a concern resulting from a complaint, or an incident occurs concerning patient safety.

NHS Wales has introduced the concept of redress, where there is an obligation of NHS organisations to investigate complaints or concerns to assess if there is qualifying liability and therefore the right for compensation.

steps.what: An official Ministry of Justice page lets a patient search for legal aid advisers for clinical negligence in England and Wales. The page found is an adviser finder rather than a full public eligibility checker, and it says the adviser will ask about the problem and finances to work out if legal aid is available.
steps.appliesIf: The patient wants to check for legal aid for a clinical negligence matter in England or Wales.
alternatives: Private funding such as no win no fee with a solicitor
missing: Whether the case fits legal aid scope

sources.quote: Search for official legal aid advisers in England and Wales.
We'll show you a list of legal advisers.
When you contact the adviser they'll ask about your problem and finances to work out if you can get legal aid.

steps.what: To find a solicitor for a clinical negligence case in Wales, use the Law Society's official 'Find a Solicitor' service for England and Wales. Its page says you can filter by legal issue and by postcode, town or country, which lets a patient search for clinical negligence solicitors near Cardiff or elsewhere in Wales.
steps.appliesIf: The patient wants a solicitor regulated in England and Wales.
alternatives: Ministry of Justice legal aid adviser finder for clinical negligence
missing: Whether the patient needs Welsh-speaking service
Whether legal aid or no win no fee is needed

steps.what: The official Welsh Government page says all NICE guidelines and quality standards are available to use in Wales, though most are not mandatory. That makes NICE the main published national clinical guidance body relevant to emergency care here, subject to Welsh legislation.
steps.appliesIf: Looking for national clinical guidance used in NHS Wales.
alternatives: Health Board local policies and pathways

sources.quote: We have an agreement that all NICE guidelines and quality standards are available to use in Wales.
Except for technology appraisal guidance (TAGs), their use is not mandatory.
All NICE guidance used in Wales is subject to Welsh legislation.

steps.what: Llais is the free independent body in Wales that helps people have a voice in health and social care and has pages for making a complaint or raising a concern. For this patient's area, the local service is Llais Cardiff & The Vale.
steps.appliesIf: The patient wants free independent help with an NHS complaint or concern in Wales.

steps.what: To get a copy of your own medical records from Cardiff and Vale University Health Board, the official pages say to contact or write to the Health Records Department. The site gives a dedicated records email and phone number, and points to the Health Board's access-to-health-records information rather than an online request form.
